package_info.why_malicious: Not a malicious package, but the use of SHA1 for artifact integrity is now considered insecure due to proven collision attacks. This creates a potential security risk where attackers could impersonate artifacts.

execution_context.file_location: Artifactory database and binary store (checksum mapping)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: SHA1(file_contents) -> 160-bit hash stored as artifact fingerprint
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When an artifact is uploaded or downloaded, the system calculates its SHA1 hash and uses this as a unique identifier for storage and integrity validation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: SHA1 is now cryptographically broken; attackers can create two different files with the same SHA1 hash (collision), allowing artifact impersonation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects a hash to uniquely identify a file. With SHA1 collisions, this uniqueness is lost, breaking the security model.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: SHA1 was previously legitimate for integrity checks before collision attacks became practical.
key_indicators: Use of SHA1 for artifact integrity
Reliance on a broken hash function for security

attack_chain.action: Attacker generates two files with the same SHA1 hash (collision).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker uploads a malicious artifact with the same SHA1 as a legitimate one.

attack_chain.action: Malicious artifact is stored and referenced by SHA1 in Artifactory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users downloading the artifact may receive the malicious file instead of the legitimate one.

attack_chain.action: Artifact integrity validation passes (SHA1 matches), but the file is not what was expected.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential compromise of systems relying on artifact integrity.

behavioral_signatures: Artifacts with identical SHA1 hashes but different content
Unexpected artifact content with valid SHA1 checksum
file_indicators: Artifacts with mismatched SHA1 and SHA-256 checksums
network_indicators: N/A (attack is local to repository and artifact storage/validation)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for artifacts with duplicate SHA1 hashes but differing SHA-256 hashes. Flag any artifact uploads where the SHA1 hash already exists for a different file. Transition to using SHA-256 for all artifact integrity checks and storage mappings to prevent collision-based impersonation attacks.
